chapter: Louis Armstrong and leaving New Orleans
title: Oliver and Noone leaving for Chicago
summary: Ory's players Joe Oliver and Jimmie Noone took Chicago jobs, and he gave them $10 each.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah, after all of it, I had an offer to go to Chicago, you see. And that time I had the two halls, you know.
He was making too much money, Louie?

All the $50 of a week in Chicago, and $300, $400 a night off my dance with you. And working on wrestling. I said, why? You go out of business, go wait for someone for now. Maybe in Chicago. So Joe Alva and Jimmy Noon was with me then. He said, we'd like to go to Chicago. I said, you want a job? I said, here's a telegram. He's right. So they went? They took the job. They didn't have raise enough to get coffee from the man, Joe and Jimmy. I said, did you guys get any of your transportation to get some advance money? He said, no. He said, we got our family. I'm going to get the same thing to eat. So I give off them $10 a piece, you know, and buy you lunch. Good luck to you.
Yeah. I went to the station with them.

I found I didn't have any money. I only had money enough to take them to Chicago. They're all the money. Should have gotten, you know, a few hundred dollars in advance money. Take them then, you know, so they could live. So I give each one of them $10 each. Lots of money, you know, because I played money.
